name: Roland Pierce
home: the western blocks near Ferry Street Rooms
life: “I still remember a painted face turning familiar on my daily commute.” Monday often includes a stop at the steps at Pier Beach, where Roland watches the working part of the waterfront before turning toward the open water.
voice: I wanted a mural until the survivor told me she would have to pass her face twice every day.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a pale blue work shirt and a knotted piece of sail thread on a key ring. Roland has a round face with a pronounced chin, with a blunt cut just below the ears. Roland draws small circles on a tabletop while waiting during a conversation.
personality: Roland is patient with a person learning and fiercely impatient with somebody pretending to know. A half-finished job left where a beginner can see it is an invitation, as far as Roland is concerned.
agenda: To get the survivor's consent before designing any mural.
family: Rowan Roman is Roland’s older cousin. Roland asks what the birthday guest would like this year. Rowan remembers the birthdays. A present that was perfect at sixteen may be completely wrong at forty. They take the trouble of finding out. Asked about *The waiting-room plant*, Rowan says, “My partner and I argued about who kept it alive.”
connections: Lee Ingram. The survivor can choose whether a picture should mark a road they must travel every day.

reactions.response: Roland lets the family make its own guest list and keeps press questions away from the table.
